chunks.title: Cloud Compute
chunks.text: Cloud Compute (infrastructure). GPU and CPU cloud services for training and inference, including managed GPU provisioning, cluster scheduling, and cloud-native ML platforms. Open-source orchestrators (Ray, SkyPilot, Volcano) cover scheduling and multi-cloud provisioning, but managed GPU availability and pricing remain dominated by hyperscalers. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Communication Libs
chunks.text: Communication Libs (infrastructure). Libraries for distributed computing across machines — collective operations, gradient synchronization, and inter-node communication for training at scale. NCCL and Gloo are open and widely used, but tightly coupled to NVIDIA hardware. Cross-vendor distributed training remains fragmented. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Compilers
chunks.text: Compilers (infrastructure). Tools that optimize models for specific hardware — graph compilers, kernel generators, and model conversion pipelines (TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, TVM, Triton). Open compilers (TVM, Triton, MLIR) are viable but lag behind vendor-optimized stacks (TensorRT, XLA) in production performance and hardware coverage. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Firmware Drivers
chunks.text: Firmware Drivers (infrastructure). Low-level software that interfaces with accelerator hardware — CUDA, ROCm, Metal, and driver-level APIs. CUDA dominates with no open equivalent. ROCm is open but AMD-only. Limited direct repo coverage — most firmware is proprietary. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Hardware Chips
chunks.text: Hardware Chips (infrastructure). AI-specific chips and accelerators — GPUs, TPUs, custom ASICs, and neuromorphic hardware. Hardware is inherently proprietary. Open efforts (RISC-V AI extensions, OpenTPU designs) are early-stage. NVIDIA, Google, and custom silicon vendors lead. Maturity: Early stage. Gap score: 2.

chunks.title: ML Frameworks
chunks.text: ML Frameworks (infrastructure). Core deep learning frameworks — PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, MLX — providing tensor operations, autograd, and training loops. PyTorch and JAX are the dominant training frameworks and both fully open. This is the strongest layer in the open-source AI stack. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Storage
chunks.text: Storage (infrastructure). Data storage and retrieval for large-scale ML — data loaders, distributed file systems, vector databases, and dataset management. Open tools exist (MinIO, LanceDB, WebDataset) but managed storage and retrieval at scale is dominated by cloud vendor offerings. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Evaluation Code
chunks.text: Evaluation Code (model_code). Scripts, harnesses, and frameworks for benchmarking model performance — HELM, lm-evaluation-harness, EleutherAI eval tools. Open eval harnesses are widely used and many closed providers publish results on them. Gap is in proprietary internal eval suites that closed labs use but don't release. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Finetuning Code
chunks.text: Finetuning Code (model_code). Code for adapting pretrained models to specific tasks — PEFT, LoRA, TRL, QLoRA, and fine-tuning frameworks. Open fine-tuning tools (PEFT, TRL, Axolotl) are production-grade. Closed labs have internal tooling but the open ecosystem is catching up quickly. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Inference Code
chunks.text: Inference Code (model_code). Code for running models in production — vLLM, TGI, llama.cpp, and inference engines optimized for latency and throughput. vLLM and TGI are best-in-class inference engines used by both open and closed providers. Strong open-source position. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Model Architecture
chunks.text: Model Architecture (model_code). Neural network structure definitions — attention mechanisms, transformer variants, mixture-of-experts, state-space models. Architecture innovation is published in papers but leading labs (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic) keep production architectures proprietary. Open reproductions lag by months. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Supporting Libraries
chunks.text: Supporting Libraries (model_code). Utility libraries for tokenization, data loading, prompt formatting, and other model-adjacent tooling. HuggingFace tokenizers, datasets, and safetensors are the standard. Open-source dominates this layer. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Training Code
chunks.text: Training Code (model_code). End-to-end training pipelines and scripts — Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, Composer, NeMo, and distributed training infrastructure. Open training stacks (DeepSpeed, Megatron, NeMo) are used to train frontier-class models. The code is open even when the resulting weights aren't. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Benchmark Eval Data
chunks.text: Benchmark Eval Data (model_datasets). Standard datasets for measuring model performance — MMLU, HellaSwag, HumanEval, and domain-specific evaluation sets. Most major benchmarks are publicly available. Gap is in proprietary internal test sets that closed labs maintain. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Data Preprocessing
chunks.text: Data Preprocessing (model_datasets). Tools for cleaning, filtering, deduplicating, and preparing training data — annotation platforms, data pipelines, and quality filters. Open tools (Label Studio, Argilla, datatrove) are viable but enterprise-grade data pipelines at scale remain a closed-source strength. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Preference Alignment Data
chunks.text: Preference Alignment Data (model_datasets). Human feedback data for RLHF, DPO, and alignment — preference pairs, reward model training sets, and constitutional AI datasets. Open preference datasets (Open Assistant, Nectar, UltraFeedback) are substantial. Closed labs generate proprietary RLHF data but open alternatives are competitive. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Pretraining Data
chunks.text: Pretraining Data (model_datasets). Large-scale corpora used to train foundation models — Common Crawl, The Pile, RedPajama, FineWeb, and web-scale text datasets. Open corpora exist but are smaller and less curated than what closed labs use. Data quality and curation at frontier scale remains a closed advantage. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Synthetic Data
chunks.text: Synthetic Data (model_datasets). Machine-generated data for training augmentation — distillation outputs, synthetic instruction sets, and data generation pipelines. Closed labs generate high-quality synthetic data from their own frontier models. Open tools (distilabel, Cosmopedia) are emerging but lag in quality. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Base Pretrained
chunks.text: Base Pretrained (model_weights). Foundation model weights before fine-tuning — Llama, Mistral, Falcon, Gemma, and other base model releases. Open base models (Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen) are competitive with closed frontiers on many benchmarks. The gap has narrowed significantly since 2023. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Compressed Weights
chunks.text: Compressed Weights (model_weights). Quantized, pruned, or distilled models optimized for efficiency — GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ formats and compressed model variants. Open quantization tools are strong (llama.cpp, GPTQ) but closed providers optimize internally with proprietary techniques. Open models often rely on community quantization. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Domain Weights
chunks.text: Domain Weights (model_weights). Models fine-tuned for specific fields — medical (Med-PaLM), legal, financial, scientific, and code-specialized models. Domain models require specialized data that closed providers often have through partnerships. Open domain models exist but coverage is uneven. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Finetuned Chat
chunks.text: Finetuned Chat (model_weights). Instruction-tuned and chat-optimized model weights — Llama Chat, Vicuna, Zephyr, and RLHF-aligned conversational models. Closed chat models (GPT-4, Claude) still lead on safety, instruction-following, and user experience. Open chat models are rapidly improving. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Multimodal Weights
chunks.text: Multimodal Weights (model_weights). Models handling multiple modalities — vision-language (LLaVA, GPT-4V), audio-language, video, and cross-modal models. Open multimodal models (LLaVA, Whisper, CLIP) are competitive. Video and real-time multimodal remain closed-led. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Deployment
chunks.text: Deployment (product_ux). Tools for serving and scaling models in production — containerization, model serving platforms, API gateways, and deployment automation. Open deployment tools (BentoML, Seldon, KServe) are production-grade. MLOps deployment is a strong open-source area. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Orchestration Agents
chunks.text: Orchestration Agents (product_ux). Frameworks for building AI agents — LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, and tool-use orchestration libraries. Agent frameworks are overwhelmingly open-source. The gap is in production reliability and enterprise features, not availability. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Output Settings
chunks.text: Output Settings (product_ux). Controls for structured output — temperature, response format, JSON mode, function calling schemas, and generation constraints. Closed APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic) lead in structured output reliability. Open tools (Outlines, Instructor) are catching up but less battle-tested. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: System Prompt
chunks.text: System Prompt (product_ux). System-level prompt configuration and management — prompt templates, prompt versioning, and system message tooling. Prompt management is fragmented in open source. Closed platforms bundle prompt engineering directly into their APIs. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Telemetry Observability
chunks.text: Telemetry Observability (product_ux). Monitoring, logging, tracing, and debugging for LLM applications — LangSmith, Langfuse, Phoenix, and OpenTelemetry integrations. Open observability tools exist (Langfuse, Phoenix) but closed platforms (LangSmith, Datadog LLM) offer more integrated experiences. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: UI & API
chunks.text: UI & API (product_ux). User-facing interfaces and API endpoints — chat UIs, playground apps, API wrappers, and developer portals. Open chat UIs (Open WebUI, LibreChat) exist but lack the polish and integration of ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini interfaces. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Data Documentation
chunks.text: Data Documentation (documentation). Data cards, provenance records, and lineage documentation — Croissant, dataset cards, and data governance tooling. Open standards (Croissant, HF dataset cards) exist but adoption is inconsistent. Closed providers document data provenance selectively. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Eval Results
chunks.text: Eval Results (documentation). Published benchmark results, leaderboards, and comparative evaluations — Open LLM Leaderboard, Chatbot Arena, and results publishing. Leaderboards are open but results are often self-reported. Independent evaluation infrastructure is underfunded. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Model Cards
chunks.text: Model Cards (documentation). Standardized model documentation — capabilities, limitations, intended use, training data, and ethical considerations. Model card tooling exists but quality varies wildly. Closed providers publish polished cards; many open models ship with minimal documentation. Maturity: Viable, but fragmented. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Sample Outputs & Demos
chunks.text: Sample Outputs & Demos (documentation). Example outputs, interactive demos, and showcase applications that demonstrate model capabilities. Open-source demos (Gradio, Streamlit, HF Spaces) are a unique strength. The demo ecosystem is overwhelmingly open. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Code Licenses
chunks.text: Code Licenses (licensing). License terms for source code — license scanning, compliance tooling, and open-source license management. License scanning tools exist but AI-specific code licensing (training code, fine-tuning scripts) has unresolved questions. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Dataset Licenses
chunks.text: Dataset Licenses (licensing). License terms for training data — data licensing frameworks, consent documentation, and rights management. Open data licensing is more transparent than closed. CDLA, ODC, and CC frameworks are well-established. Maturity: Strong. Gap score: 4.

chunks.title: Terms of Service
chunks.text: Terms of Service (licensing). Usage policies, acceptable use terms, and terms-of-service analysis tooling for AI products. Almost no open-source tooling for ToS analysis or comparison. Closed providers set terms unilaterally. Maturity: Early stage. Gap score: 2.

chunks.title: Weight Licenses
chunks.text: Weight Licenses (licensing). License terms for model weights — Llama Community License, RAIL, OpenRAIL, and weight-specific licensing frameworks. Weight licensing is actively evolving. Open frameworks (RAIL, Llama license) exist but lack standardization. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Access & Release
chunks.text: Access & Release (safeguards). How models are distributed and access-controlled — staged releases, gated downloads, and responsible disclosure practices. Closed providers have established release processes. Open model releases vary from careful (Llama) to permissive (community fine-tunes). Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Auditing & Reporting
chunks.text: Auditing & Reporting (safeguards). Third-party audits, transparency reports, bias assessments, and safety auditing infrastructure. Auditing tooling is sparse. Closed providers publish transparency reports; open models rarely undergo systematic safety audits. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Governance
chunks.text: Governance (safeguards). Decision-making structures, oversight mechanisms, and AI governance tooling — policy frameworks and organizational governance. AI governance is mostly institutional, not software. Open governance tools are early-stage. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Moderation
chunks.text: Moderation (safeguards). Content filtering, safety guardrails, toxicity detection, and content moderation systems. Open moderation tools (Llama Guard, Perspective API) exist but closed providers have more sophisticated multi-layered systems. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: Safety & Alignment
chunks.text: Safety & Alignment (safeguards). Techniques to align model behavior with human values — RLHF, constitutional AI, red teaming, and alignment research tooling. Alignment research is published openly but production alignment techniques (RLHF at scale, constitutional AI) are practiced primarily by closed labs. Maturity: Viable. Gap score: 3.

chunks.title: model-router (Routing)
chunks.text: model-router — Routing layer. By Arch-Router · Katanemo. Status: building. Planned: route each query to the right open model by task (Arch-Router-1.5B). One model serves every answer today; provider routing (LiteLLM) is {routingProvider}.

chunks.title: {modelShort} (Model)
chunks.text: {modelShort} — Model layer. By Swiss AI Initiative (SwissAI). Status: live. Open-weights Swiss foundation model (text-only today; multimodal incoming). Multilingual, open training data. Served checkpoint: {servedCheckpoint}. Provenance: open weights · HuggingFace · trained on CSCS.

chunks.title: CSCS 🇨🇭 (Compute)
chunks.text: CSCS 🇨🇭 — Compute layer. By Swiss National Supercomputing Centre. Status: live. Sovereign public compute — owned by the public, not a company. Apertus was trained here; it's the production serving target too ({cscsServingNote}). Provenance: public infrastructure · Switzerland.

chunks.title: LUMI 🇫🇮 (Compute)
chunks.text: LUMI 🇫🇮 — Compute layer. By CSC, Finland. Status: live. EuroHPC sovereign compute pool — a production serving target for the public stack. Provenance: public infrastructure · EuroHPC.

chunks.title: toxic-bert (Safety)
chunks.text: toxic-bert — Safety layer. By Unitary · Detoxify. Status: live. Apache-2.0 toxicity classifier — screens every message before it reaches the model. Flags toxic or abusive language (not all harmful requests). Provenance: open safety classifier.

chunks.title: Osprey (Safety)
chunks.text: Osprey — Safety layer. By ROOST.tech. Status: building. Request-path abuse detection with reviewable logs — building. Provenance: open moderation tooling.

chunks.title: Web search (Tools)
chunks.text: Web search — Tools layer. By Wikipedia · Marginalia. Status: live. Open-knowledge search over Wikipedia (open public knowledge) + Marginalia (open independent index), grounding answers with cited sources. A Google-scale open web index is still the honest gap. Provenance: open knowledge + open independent index.

chunks.title: File upload (Tools)
chunks.text: File upload — Tools layer. By Docling · pgvector. Status: building. Open document parsing + retrieval over open vector stores — building. File attach is wired but turned off for the alpha; parsing isn't built yet.

chunks.title: Voice (Tools)
chunks.text: Voice — Tools layer. By open invitation. Status: wanted. Talk to it out loud. Not part of the open stack here yet — an open invitation, not a closed door.

chunks.title: Image generation (Tools)
chunks.text: Image generation — Tools layer. By open invitation. Status: wanted. Make images from a prompt. Open projects exist; nobody has wired one in here yet.

chunks.title: Nous Hermes (Agent)
chunks.text: Nous Hermes — Agent layer. By Nous Research. Status: building. Hosted agent service — developer API only for the alpha. Provenance: open agent models · API-only for alpha.

chunks.title: Computer use (Agent)
chunks.text: Computer use — Agent layer. By open invitation. Status: wanted. Let the AI act in apps and the browser on your behalf.

chunks.title: Memory (Agent)
chunks.text: Memory — Agent layer. By open invitation. Status: wanted. Remember context across conversations.

chunks.title: local-culture (Community)
chunks.text: local-culture — Community layer. By open invitation. Status: gap. Community self-configuration of a live deployment. Not built yet — an open gap, not a promise. This is where a contribution would land.

chunks.title: AI Potluck
chunks.text: AI Potluck is the open, map-grounded chat from Current AI, a nonprofit coalition assembling a full-stack, open-source alternative to closed AI from open components. Current AI serves open models here, it does not build them. For the current list of partners or how the project is funded, point people to the project website rather than naming specific partners, funders, or funding sources.
